study: Fully-recursive Karatsuba vs schoolbook multiplier, measured in hardware. Does the algorithm's asymptotic multiply-operation advantage translate into a hardware win?
answer: No, at synthesizable widths. Recursive Karatsuba is worse on area, transistors, AND logic depth (speed) at every width 8-64b. The recombination-adder overhead of full recursion exceeds the multiply savings in silicon.
tool: Yosys 0.23 + ABC (technology mapping to sky130 HD). Mapping: 'abc -liberty <lib> -fast' (identical for both designs). NOTE: the DEFAULT abc script hangs on the recursive netlist (berkeley-abc spins > 4 h); -fast maps it in ~7 s. This is itself a finding: the recursive structure is pathological for the default mapper.
transistor_source: per-cell MOSFET count parsed from the sky130 cell SPICE (sky130_fd_sc_hd.spice); cross-checked (fa_1 = 28T, matches the mirror-adder full adder).
depth_source: combinational longest input-to-output path in gate levels, computed from the mapped JSON netlist (parse_depth.py). A synthesis-level delay proxy: no wire load, no placement, no signoff STA. ltp and ABC report no usable delay for a purely combinational module in this toolchain.
recursive_generator: karat_recursive.py, base case schoolbook at w<=4. Proven km8 == a*b for all inputs by Yosys SAT (no model found).
findings: AREA/TRANSISTORS: recursive is larger at every width, converging toward parity as width grows (transistor ratio 1.67 -> 1.04); the area crossover sits just past 64 bits.

DEPTH/SPEED: recursive is ~2x deeper at 8b and the gap WIDENS to 2.53x at 64b. Schoolbook depth grows near-logarithmically (ABC balances it into a tree); recursive depth grows fast because the recombination-adder chain deepens at every recursion level.

The asymptotic advantage of Karatsuba is in multiply-OPERATION count (O(n^1.585) vs O(n^2)) -- a sequential/software property. It does NOT become fewer transistors or lower delay in combinational hardware at these widths.

Deeper recursion is worse, not better: one-level Karatsuba reached ~parity/modest area win by ~15b, while FULL recursion is worse on every axis through 64b. The optimal recursion depth for hardware is shallow.
The hardware speed play for multipliers is tree reduction (Wallace 1964, Dadda 1965), not Karatsuba. Karatsuba is an operation-count optimization for very large (software) multiplies.
